# PR-1: PR-1: Customer onboarding and identity checks (KYC)

**Story.** As a new customer, I want to register my personal identity details for compliance review so that once verified I am eligible to open a bank account, while ensuring underage or unverified applicants are blocked.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Domain types exist in Bank.Modules.Customers.Domain: enum KycStatus { Pending, Verified, Rejected }, sealed class Customer (with parameterless constructor, Id, FullName, Email, [Pii] NationalId, [Pii] DateOfBirth, Status with private setter defaulting to Pending, DecidedBy, RegisteredAt, Verify(string officerId), Reject(string officerId)), and sealed record IDomainEvent types CustomerRegistered(string CustomerId, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt), CustomerVerified(string CustomerId, string VerifiedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt), and CustomerRejected(string CustomerId, string RejectedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt).
- [ ] Customer.Verify(officerId) and Customer.Reject(officerId) transition Status from Pending to Verified or Rejected respectively and set DecidedBy to officerId; invoking either method when Status is not Pending throws InvalidOperationException.
- [ ] ICustomerService.RegisterAsync registers a Customer for the signed-in user (Id = ICurrentUser.UserId) with Status = KycStatus.Pending and RegisteredAt = IClock.UtcNow, persists it to BankDbContext.Customers, and publishes CustomerRegistered via IEventBus.
- [ ] ICustomerService.RegisterAsync throws ArgumentException if FullName, Email, or NationalId is null/empty/whitespace, or if the applicant is under 18 years old on IClock.UtcNow's date (turning 18 on that exact calendar date is accepted; one day younger is rejected); it throws InvalidOperationException if a Customer with ICurrentUser.UserId already exists.
- [ ] ICustomerService.VerifyAsync(customerId) and RejectAsync(customerId) throw UnauthorizedAccessException if the caller does not have the Compliance role or if ICurrentUser.UserId equals customerId (no self-verification or self-rejection), and throw KeyNotFoundException if customerId does not exist.
- [ ] On successful VerifyAsync or RejectAsync, the Customer status and DecidedBy are persisted to BankDbContext.Customers and CustomerVerified or CustomerRejected is published via IEventBus.
- [ ] ICustomerService.GetAsync(customerId) returns the matching Customer from BankDbContext.Customers or null when not found.
- [ ] KycAccountOpeningRule implements IAccountOpeningRule and throws UnauthorizedAccessException if the target customer does not exist in BankDbContext.Customers or has Status other than KycStatus.Verified.
- [ ] BankDbContext declares DbSet<Customer> Customers above the // TABLES: marker, CustomersModule registers ICustomerService (CustomerService) and IAccountOpeningRule (KycAccountOpeningRule), and AddCustomersModule is registered in Program.cs above // MODULES:.
- [ ] HTTP endpoints are exposed with [ApiController] and explicit [Authorize(Policy = ...)] attributes: POST api/customers (Customer policy, derives user id solely from ICurrentUser), GET api/customers/me (Customer policy, returns current user's customer), POST api/customers/{id}/verify (Compliance policy), and POST api/customers/{id}/reject (Compliance policy).
- [ ] NationalId and DateOfBirth are marked with [Pii] on Customer and never appear in domain events, exception messages, or logs; all timestamps and age checks use IClock.UtcNow rather than DateTime.Now or DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.

## Out of scope
- Integration with external identity verification providers, document uploads, or automated KYC/sanctions/PEP screening.
- Updating customer profile or PII fields after registration, or re-applying after a Rejected status.
- Compliance officer queue, search, or list endpoints for browsing Pending registrations.
- Customer notifications (email, SMS, or push) upon registration, verification, or rejection.
- Account creation endpoints, deposit/transfer flows, or any ledger/monetary operations.
- Customer deletion or GDPR data erasure workflows.

## Risks
- Self-verification bypass: if VerifyAsync or RejectAsync fails to enforce both the Compliance role and officerId != customerId, an insider or compromised compliance account could approve their own KYC.
- Unverified account opening: if KycAccountOpeningRule is not wired as IAccountOpeningRule or fails open for missing, Pending, or Rejected customers, unverified or underage users could open accounts.
- PII exposure: logging request bodies, embedding NationalId or DateOfBirth in exception messages, or adding PII fields to domain events would leak sensitive personal data.
- Incorrect age calculation: using DateTime.UtcNow instead of IClock.UtcNow or approximating 18 years as 365 * 18 days could allow underage applicants on leap years or wrongly reject eligible 18-year-olds.
- Audit trail corruption: allowing direct mutation of Status or DecidedBy without going through Pending-only domain methods could overwrite compliance decisions.
- Identity spoofing: trusting a user id from the HTTP request body instead of ICurrentUser.UserId in POST api/customers could allow one user to register or block another user's identity.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Modules.Customers.Domain:
  enum KycStatus { Pending, Verified, Rejected }
  sealed class Customer { string Id (the user id, primary key); string FullName; string Email; [Pii] string NationalId;
                          [Pii] DateOnly DateOfBirth; KycStatus Status { get; private set; } (starts Pending); string? DecidedBy;
                          DateTimeOffset RegisteredAt;
                          void Verify(string officerId); void Reject(string officerId) }   // only from Pending, else InvalidOperationException
  sealed record CustomerRegistered(string CustomerId, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record CustomerVerified(string CustomerId, string VerifiedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record CustomerRejected(string CustomerId, string RejectedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
namespace Bank.Modules.Customers.Application:
  sealed record RegisterCustomerRequest(string FullName, string Email, string NationalId, DateOnly DateOfBirth)
  interface ICustomerService {
    Task<Customer> RegisterAsync(RegisterCustomerRequest request, CancellationToken ct = default);  // for the signed-in user;
        // already registered -> InvalidOperationException; under 18 on IClock's date -> ArgumentException; empty fields -> ArgumentException
    Task<Customer> VerifyAsync(string customerId, CancellationToken ct = default);   // compliance officer only, never themselves -> UnauthorizedAccessException; unknown -> KeyNotFoundException
    Task<Customer> RejectAsync(string customerId, CancellationToken ct = default);   // same rules as VerifyAsync
    Task<Customer?> GetAsync(string customerId, CancellationToken ct = default); }
  sealed class CustomerService(BankDbContext db, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock, IEventBus bus) : ICustomerService
  sealed class KycAccountOpeningRule(BankDbContext db) : IAccountOpeningRule   // not Verified (or unknown) -> UnauthorizedAccessException
CustomersModule registers ICustomerService and KycAccountOpeningRule as IAccountOpeningRule.
BankDbContext gets: DbSet<Customer> Customers
HTTP: POST api/customers (register yourself), GET api/customers/me, POST api/customers/{id}/verify, POST api/customers/{id}/reject (Compliance policy)
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Customers/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs`
- `src/Bank.Api/Program.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ New customers register with their full name, e-mail, national identity number and date of birth. Customers must be at least 18. A compliance officer reviews each registration and verifies or rejects it; nobody can verify themselves. A customer who is not verified cannot open an account. National id and date of birth are personal data and must never appear in events, logs or messages.

# PR-2: PR-2: Implement same-currency customer payments between bank accounts

**Story.** As an authenticated bank customer, I want to transfer whole-cent amounts in the same currency from one of my own accounts to any other account in the bank using an idempotency key and within the daily transfer limit, so that my payments are processed safely without duplicate transfers on retries.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Authorization and Identity: Both POST api/payments and GET api/payments require the Customer policy (Policies.Customer), and PaymentService always identifies the caller using ICurrentUser.UserId rather than any user identifier from a request payload or query parameter.
- [ ] Ownership Check: Calling PayAsync where FromAccountId is not owned by ICurrentUser.UserId (verified via IAccountService) throws UnauthorizedAccessException and does not move money or persist a Payment.
- [ ] Amount Validation: Calling PayAsync with Amount less than or equal to 0, or with fractional cents (more than 2 decimal places, where Amount != Math.Round(Amount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)), throws ArgumentException and does not move money or persist a Payment.
- [ ] Currency Matching: Calling PayAsync where FromAccountId and ToAccountId have different currencies throws CurrencyMismatchException and does not move money or persist a Payment.
- [ ] Idempotency: Calling PayAsync with an IdempotencyKey already used by the same CustomerId returns the existing Payment record without calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync, without counting the amount again toward the daily limit, and without publishing another PaymentCompleted event; identical IdempotencyKey values from different customers are treated independently.
- [ ] Daily Transfer Limit: Before moving money, PayAsync sums the CustomerId's completed payments whose CreatedAt falls within the current UTC calendar day (using IClock.UtcNow); if that sum plus request.Amount exceeds BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit, PayAsync throws DailyLimitExceededException and does not move money or persist a Payment, whereas a total exactly equal to BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit is permitted.
- [ ] Insufficient Funds: If the source account has insufficient funds when posting via ILedger.PostTransferAsync, InsufficientFundsException is thrown and no Completed Payment is persisted.
- [ ] Ledger Posting and Persistence: On valid payment execution, money moves exclusively via ILedger.PostTransferAsync(FromAccountId, ToAccountId, Amount, Reference) without modifying Account.Balance directly; the Payment is saved to BankDbContext.Payments with Status = PaymentStatus.Completed (updated through an entity method with a private setter), TransferId set to the returned ledger transfer ID, Currency set to the accounts' currency, CustomerId = ICurrentUser.UserId, and CreatedAt = IClock.UtcNow.
- [ ] Domain Event: Upon completing a new payment, PaymentService publishes PaymentCompleted(PaymentId, CustomerId, Amount, Currency, OccurredAt) using IClock.UtcNow via IEventBus.PublishAsync, containing no personal data such as Reference or customer PII.
- [ ] Querying Payments: GET api/payments calls IPaymentService.ForCustomerAsync with ICurrentUser.UserId and returns only the authenticated customer's Payment records.
- [ ] Module Registration and Public Contract: The Payments module implements the agreed Domain types (PaymentStatus, Payment, PaymentCompleted) and Application types (PaymentRequest, DailyLimitExceededException, IPaymentService, PaymentService), adds DbSet<Payment> Payments to BankDbContext, and registers via PaymentsModule.AddPaymentsModule in Program.cs.

## Out of scope
- Cross-currency payments and foreign exchange (FX) conversion.
- Payment holding, fraud or compliance review workflows, or rejection state transitions (PaymentStatus.Held and PaymentStatus.Rejected).
- Scheduled, future-dated, or recurring payments.
- External bank transfers outside the bank's own accounts.
- Payment cancellation, reversals, refunds, or transaction fees.
- Customer-specific daily transfer limits overriding BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit.
- Staff, Compliance, or Admin endpoints for viewing or managing customer payments.

## Risks
- Concurrent Duplicate Requests: Two simultaneous requests with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey could both pass an application-level existence check and trigger duplicate ledger transfers unless enforced by a unique database constraint on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey).
- Daily Limit Race Condition: Concurrent payments from the same customer could each read the same prior daily total and collectively exceed BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit if not serialized or checked transactionally.
- Partial Failure Across Ledger and Payments Storage: If ILedger.PostTransferAsync commits a transfer but persisting the Payment fails (or vice versa), the customer's balance and payment history become inconsistent.
- Idempotency Key Reuse with Different Parameters: If a client reuses an IdempotencyKey with a different ToAccountId or Amount, returning the original Payment could mask a client bug or mislead the customer.
- Broken Access Control (IDOR): Relying on a caller-supplied CustomerId instead of ICurrentUser.UserId in either PayAsync or GET api/payments could allow unauthorized transfers or exposure of other customers' payment histories.
- Clock and Timezone Drift: Using DateTime.Now or DateTimeOffset.UtcNow directly instead of IClock.UtcNow in UTC calendar day calculations could cause inconsistent daily limit enforcement around midnight UTC and break deterministic testing.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Modules.Payments.Domain:
  enum PaymentStatus { Completed, Held, Rejected }
  sealed class Payment { Guid Id; string IdempotencyKey; string CustomerId; Guid FromAccountId; Guid ToAccountId;
                         decimal Amount; string Currency; PaymentStatus Status; Guid? TransferId; string? Reference; DateTimeOffset CreatedAt }
  sealed record PaymentCompleted(Guid PaymentId, string CustomerId, decimal Amount, string Currency, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
namespace Bank.Modules.Payments.Application:
  sealed record PaymentRequest(string IdempotencyKey, Guid FromAccountId, Guid ToAccountId, decimal Amount, string? Reference)
  sealed class DailyLimitExceededException : InvalidOperationException
  interface IPaymentService {
    Task<Payment> PayAsync(PaymentRequest request, CancellationToken ct = default);
        // from-account not owned by the caller -> UnauthorizedAccessException; amount <= 0 or not whole cents -> ArgumentException;
        // same caller + same key -> the existing payment, no new money movement; over the daily limit -> DailyLimitExceededException;
        // insufficient funds -> InsufficientFundsException (from the Ledger); different currencies -> CurrencyMismatchException
    Task<IReadOnlyList<Payment>> ForCustomerAsync(string customerId, CancellationToken ct = default); }
  sealed class PaymentService(BankDbContext db, ILedger ledger, IAccountService accounts, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock,
                              BankSettings settings, IEventBus bus) : IPaymentService
BankDbContext gets: DbSet<Payment> Payments
HTTP: POST api/payments, GET api/payments (Customer policy)
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Payments/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs`
- `src/Bank.Api/Program.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ A customer can send money from one of their own accounts to any other account in the bank. Every payment request carries an idempotency key chosen by the app; if the same customer sends the same key again (for example after a timeout), the bank returns the first payment and does not move money again. Customers can send at most the daily transfer limit from BankSettings per calendar day (UTC). Amounts must be positive whole cents. In this PR both accounts must have the same currency.

# PR-3: PR-3: Currency exchange service and cross-currency payments

**Story.** As a bank customer, I want to make payments between accounts in different supported currencies (EUR, SEK, USD) with consistent exchange rates and EUR-equivalent daily transfer limits, so that I can transfer money across currencies reliably.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Create the Fx module under src/Bank.Api/Modules/Fx/ with Bank.Modules.Fx.Application.IFxService and sealed class FxService : IFxService (parameterless constructor), and register it via FxModule.AddFxModule in Program.cs above the // MODULES: line.
- [ ] IFxService.Rate(fromCurrency, toCurrency) returns 1 for identical supported currencies (EUR, SEK, USD) and throws ArgumentException if either currency is null, empty, or not one of EUR, SEK, USD.
- [ ] IFxService.Rate uses fixed base rates 1 EUR = 11.50 SEK and 1 EUR = 1.08 USD; inverse pairs use 1 / 11.50 (SEK to EUR) and 1 / 1.08 (USD to EUR); cross pairs triangulate through EUR (SEK to USD converts SEK to EUR then EUR to USD; USD to SEK converts USD to EUR then EUR to SEK).
- [ ] IFxService.Convert(amount, fromCurrency, toCurrency) converts the amount using the pair rate (triangulating through EUR for non-EUR pairs) and rounds the final result to 2 decimal places using Math.Round(..., 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero); throws ArgumentException for unknown currencies.
- [ ] Payment entity in Bank.Modules.Payments.Domain adds public settable properties decimal CreditedAmount, string CreditedCurrency, and decimal Rate; for same-currency payments CreditedAmount equals Amount, CreditedCurrency equals payee/payer currency, and Rate equals 1.
- [ ] PaymentService accepts IFxService as a constructor parameter immediately after BankSettings.
- [ ] Cross-currency payments between supported currencies (EUR, SEK, USD) are allowed and no longer throw CurrencyMismatchException.
- [ ] For a cross-currency payment, PaymentService moves funds solely via ILedger.PostTransferAsync: it debits the payer account for Amount in the payer currency to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.FxClearing, payerCurrency) and credits the payee account for CreditedAmount in the payee currency from BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.FxClearing, payeeCurrency); Account.Balance is never modified directly.
- [ ] For a same-currency payment, funds continue to move directly from the payer account to the payee account via ILedger.PostTransferAsync with CreditedAmount = Amount and Rate = 1.
- [ ] Daily transfer limit enforcement (BankSettings.DailyTransferLimit) evaluates all payments in their EUR equivalent using IFxService (converting each payment's debited amount from its currency to EUR) and rejects any payment that would cause the customer's daily total in EUR to exceed DailyTransferLimit.
- [ ] Existing security rules remain enforced: payment endpoints keep [Authorize(Policy = Policies.X)], caller identity is read only from ICurrentUser (never request body), account ownership is checked via IAccountService.IsOwnerAsync, timestamps use IClock.UtcNow, and no PII is written to logs, events, or error messages.
- [ ] Automated xUnit tests cover FxService (same currency returning 1, EUR/SEK/USD direct and inverse pairs, SEK<->USD triangulation, half-away-from-zero rounding to 2 decimals, ArgumentException on unknown currency), cross-currency PaymentService flows (including FxClearing ledger transfers and Payment properties CreditedAmount, CreditedCurrency, Rate), and EUR-equivalent daily transfer limit enforcement.

## Out of scope
- HTTP API controller or endpoints for querying FX rates or quoting currency conversions.
- Dynamic, external, or database-stored FX rates and admin endpoints to update exchange rates.
- FX spreads, conversion commissions, or FeeIncome ledger postings on currency exchange.
- Support for any currencies other than EUR, SEK, and USD.
- Historical rate tables, FX position reporting, or revaluation of FxClearing balances.

## Risks
- Partial ledger failure between the two PostTransferAsync calls (debiting payer to FxClearing succeeding while crediting payee from FxClearing fails) could leave funds stranded in FxClearing and misstate customer balances.
- Rounding or precision differences during EUR triangulation (such as rounding an intermediate EUR amount versus rounding only the final credited amount) could cause unexpected customer amounts or FxClearing ledger imbalances.
- Very small cross-currency payment amounts could round CreditedAmount down to 0.00, leading to failed zero-amount ledger postings or customer confusion.
- Inconsistent EUR conversion of prior same-day payments when computing the daily total could allow customers to bypass DailyTransferLimit or be wrongly blocked.
- Forgetting to update the database schema or seed/test data for the new Payment properties (CreditedAmount, CreditedCurrency, Rate) could cause EF Core runtime or persistence failures.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Modules.Fx.Application:
  interface IFxService {
    decimal Rate(string fromCurrency, string toCurrency);                 // same currency -> 1; unknown currency -> ArgumentException
    decimal Convert(decimal amount, string fromCurrency, string toCurrency); }   // rounded to cents, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero
  sealed class FxService : IFxService     // no constructor arguments
Payment gets: decimal CreditedAmount; string CreditedCurrency; decimal Rate   (same currency: CreditedAmount = Amount, Rate = 1)
PaymentService gets IFxService as a constructor argument (after BankSettings): cross-currency payments no longer throw CurrencyMismatchException.
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Fx/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Payments/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Program.cs`
- `src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ The bank holds EUR, SEK and USD. Add exchange rates: 1 EUR = 11.50 SEK and 1 EUR = 1.08 USD; other pairs go through EUR (SEK to USD = from SEK to EUR, then EUR to USD). Converted amounts are rounded to cents, half away from zero. Payments may now go between accounts in different currencies: the payer is debited in their currency, the payee is credited the converted amount, and the money passes through the bank's FxClearing account of each currency. The daily transfer limit now counts every payment in its EUR equivalent.

# PR-4: PR-4: Fees for cross-currency payments and pre-payment quote

**Story.** As a bank customer making a cross-currency payment, I want to see the applicable fee, exchange rate, and credited amount in a quote before paying, and have the fee charged transparently in my currency on top of the payment amount only when my balance covers the total.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A new Fees module is created under src/Bank.Api/Modules/Fees with Application/Fee.cs (sealed record Fee(decimal Amount, string Currency)), Application/IFeeCalculator.cs, Application/FeeCalculator.cs (sealed class FeeCalculator(IFxService fx) : IFeeCalculator), and FeesModule.cs registered in Program.cs above // MODULES:.
- [ ] IFeeCalculator.Quote(amount, fromCurrency, toCurrency) returns Fee(0m, fromCurrency) when fromCurrency equals toCurrency (case-insensitive).
- [ ] For cross-currency calls (fromCurrency != toCurrency) with amount > 0, IFeeCalculator.Quote calculates 0.2% of amount (amount * 0.002m), converts the 0.50 EUR minimum and 20.00 EUR maximum into fromCurrency via IFxService, rounds the raw fee and converted bounds to 2 decimal places using Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero), and clamps the fee between the converted min and max in fromCurrency.
- [ ] If amount <= 0, IFeeCalculator.Quote and IPaymentService quote/pay operations reject the request with a validation error (HTTP 400 Bad Request at the API layer).
- [ ] PaymentQuote(decimal Amount, string Currency, decimal Fee, decimal CreditedAmount, string CreditedCurrency, decimal Rate) is added to Bank.Modules.Payments.Application, and IPaymentService exposes Quote / QuoteAsync(Guid fromAccountId, Guid toAccountId, decimal amount) returning the fee, FX rate (1m for same-currency), and rounded CreditedAmount without modifying balances or persisting a Payment.
- [ ] GET api/payments/quote?from={fromAccountId}&to={toAccountId}&amount={amount} is decorated with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)], uses ICurrentUser.UserId and IAccountService.IsOwnerAsync to verify the caller owns the from account (returning 403 Forbidden if not owner and 404 Not Found if either account does not exist), and returns HTTP 200 with the PaymentQuote JSON.
- [ ] Payment entity adds a decimal Fee property persisted in BankDbContext, and PaymentService accepts IFeeCalculator in its constructor immediately after IFxService.
- [ ] When executing a payment, PaymentService checks that the payer account balance is at least amount + fee before posting any ledger transfers; if balance < amount + fee, the payment fails with insufficient funds, no Payment is completed, and zero transfers are posted to either the recipient, FxClearing, or FeeIncome.
- [ ] When a cross-currency payment succeeds with Fee > 0, PaymentService posts the fee transfer in the payer's currency via ILedger.PostTransferAsync from the payer account to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.FeeIncome, fromAccount.Currency), alongside the payment transfer(s), so the payer is debited amount + fee in total; for same-currency payments (Fee == 0), no FeeIncome transfer is posted.

## Out of scope
- Quote locking, FX rate reservation, or guaranteed quote expiration windows (execution uses live FX rates at payment time).
- Customer-tier fee discounts, fee waivers, promotional codes, or configurable fee percentages/caps in BankSettings or database.
- Charging fees on same-currency payments, loan disbursements/repayments, or internal bank transfers.
- Fee refunds or reversals on disputed or cancelled payments.
- Frontend or UI components for displaying the quote.

## Risks
- Non-atomic multi-leg ledger posting: if the principal/FX transfer succeeds and the FeeIncome transfer fails (or vice versa), customer balances and bank FeeIncome accounts will fall out of sync unless wrapped in a single database transaction and pre-validated for amount + fee.
- Rounding discrepancies: inconsistent rounding between FeeCalculator, PaymentQuote, and PaymentService (such as failing to use MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) could cause a 1-cent mismatch between the quoted fee and the debited fee.
- IDOR on quote endpoint: omitting ownership verification on the from account in GET api/payments/quote would allow an authenticated customer to enumerate other customers' account IDs and currencies.
- Rate movement between quote and execution: because quotes are non-binding, an FX rate shift before payment submission could change the converted EUR fee bounds or CreditedAmount.
- Unsupported currency handling: calling BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.FeeIncome, currency) with a currency outside EUR, SEK, or USD would fail at runtime if account currency validation is missing.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Modules.Fees.Application:
  sealed record Fee(decimal Amount, string Currency)
  interface IFeeCalculator { Fee Quote(decimal amount, string fromCurrency, string toCurrency); }
  sealed class FeeCalculator(IFxService fx) : IFeeCalculator
namespace Bank.Modules.Payments.Application:
  sealed record PaymentQuote(decimal Amount, string Currency, decimal Fee, decimal CreditedAmount, string CreditedCurrency, decimal Rate)
  IPaymentService adds: PaymentQuote Quote(Guid fromAccountId, Guid toAccountId, decimal amount)  -- async variant allowed: Task<PaymentQuote> QuoteAsync(...)
Payment gets: decimal Fee
PaymentService gets IFeeCalculator as a constructor argument (after IFxService).
HTTP: GET api/payments/quote?from=&to=&amount=
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Fees/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Payments/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Program.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ Payments in the same currency stay free. # PR-5: PR-5: Implement Debit Cards Module (Issue, Lifecycle, and Payment Authorisation)

**Story.** As a bank customer, I want to obtain a debit card for my account and freeze, unfreeze, or permanently cancel it, and as the bank acting on card network requests, I want to authorise or decline card payments against card status, per-transaction limit, and account balance while holding authorised funds in Suspense.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Module structure and registration: Cards module lives under src/Bank.Api/Modules/Cards with Api, Application, Domain folders and CardsModule.cs, registered in Program.cs above // MODULES: and DbSet<Card> Cards added to BankDbContext above // TABLES:.
- [ ] Card issuance (POST api/cards, Customer policy): Authenticated customer calls ICardService.IssueAsync(accountId). Caller ownership is verified via IAccountService.IsOwnerAsync(accountId, currentUser.UserId); non-owners receive UnauthorizedAccessException. Creates an Active Card with a generated 16-digit Number annotated with [Pii], Last4 equal to the last 4 digits of Number, PerTransactionLimit of 2000m, CustomerId from ICurrentUser.UserId, and publishes CardIssued(CardId, CustomerId, Last4, clock.UtcNow).
- [ ] Card lifecycle (POST api/cards/{id}/freeze, /unfreeze, /cancel, Customer policy): FreezeAsync, UnfreezeAsync, and CancelAsync verify card.CustomerId == currentUser.UserId via ICurrentUser (throwing UnauthorizedAccessException otherwise) and invoke Card.Freeze(), Card.Unfreeze(), or Card.Cancel().
- [ ] Card state machine: CardStatus is Active, Frozen, or Cancelled with a private setter on Card.Status. Once Cancelled, any call to Freeze(), Unfreeze(), or Cancel() throws InvalidOperationException.
- [ ] Card payment authorisation (POST api/cards/{id}/authorise, Staff policy): Calls ICardService.AuthoriseAsync(cardId, amount, merchant) with no customer ownership check. Input amount is decimal and rounded to 2 decimal places using Math.Round(amount, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero). Amounts less than or equal to 0 after rounding are rejected.
- [ ] Authorisation decline rules (returned as CardAuthorisation(false, reason, null) with HTTP 200, not thrown as errors, and publishing CardPaymentDeclined(CardId, reason, clock.UtcNow)): (1) if Card.Status is not Active, decline with reason "card not active"; (2) if rounded amount exceeds Card.PerTransactionLimit (2000m in the account currency), decline with reason "over limit"; (3) if the account lacks sufficient funds when posting the transfer, decline with reason "insufficient funds".
- [ ] Authorisation approval rules: When the card is Active, rounded amount is within 2000m, and the account has sufficient funds, funds move strictly via ILedger.PostTransferAsync from card.AccountId to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, account.Currency) for the rounded amount. Returns CardAuthorisation(true, null, transferId) and publishes CardPaymentAuthorised(CardId, roundedAmount, account.Currency, merchant, clock.UtcNow).
- [ ] PII protection and data handling: Card.Number is marked [Pii] and is never returned in any API response DTO, domain event, log message, or error message; API responses expose only Last4. All timestamps use IClock.UtcNow and Account.Balance is never modified directly.

## Out of scope
- Payment settlement, clearing, capture, refunds, or reversals out of the Suspense account.
- Custom or user-configurable per-transaction limits, daily/monthly spending caps, or ATM/cash withdrawal limits.
- PIN generation or verification, CVV/CVC handling, card expiry dates, or physical card production and shipping.
- Multi-currency card payments or FX conversion during authorisation.
- GET endpoints for listing cards or retrieving card details, and replacing or reissuing cancelled cards.
- Direct integration with external card schemes (Visa, Mastercard) or ISO 8583 messaging.

## Risks
- PII leakage: Returning Card.Number in API DTOs or logging full 16-digit card numbers would expose personal data and violate banking security standards.
- Authorization bypass or misconfiguration: Omitting ownership checks on Issue, Freeze, Unfreeze, or Cancel allows one customer to tamper with another customer's cards, while mistakenly adding an ownership check to AuthoriseAsync would break Staff/card-network authorisations.
- Double-spend / overdraft race condition: If balance verification and ILedger.PostTransferAsync are not atomic under concurrent AuthoriseAsync calls, multiple simultaneous payments could overdraw the customer's account.
- Broken terminal state enforcement: Allowing a Cancelled card to be unfrozen or used for payments enables fraudulent transactions on permanently closed cards.
- Incorrect ledger currency or error handling: Posting to Suspense in a hardcoded currency instead of the linked account's currency would corrupt ledger balances, and throwing HTTP exceptions on declines instead of returning CardAuthorisation would break card-network protocol expectations.
- Rounding discrepancies: Failing to apply MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero consistently before both the 2000m limit check and the ledger transfer could allow fractional-cent amounts to bypass limits or fail settlement.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Modules.Cards.Domain:
  enum CardStatus { Active, Frozen, Cancelled }
  sealed class Card { Guid Id; Guid AccountId; string CustomerId; [Pii] string Number (16 digits); string Last4;
                      CardStatus Status { get; private set; }; decimal PerTransactionLimit (2000);
                      void Freeze(); void Unfreeze(); void Cancel(); }   // Cancelled is final: any change after it -> InvalidOperationException
  sealed record CardIssued(Guid CardId, string CustomerId, string Last4, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record CardPaymentAuthorised(Guid CardId, decimal Amount, string Currency, string Merchant, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record CardPaymentDeclined(Guid CardId, string Reason, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
namespace Bank.Modules.Cards.Application:
  sealed record CardAuthorisation(bool Approved, string? DeclineReason, Guid? TransferId)   // reasons: "card not active", "over limit", "insufficient funds"
  interface ICardService {
    Task<Card> IssueAsync(Guid accountId, CancellationToken ct = default);   // account not owned by caller -> UnauthorizedAccessException
    Task<Card> FreezeAsync(Guid cardId, CancellationToken ct = default);     // owner only -> UnauthorizedAccessException
    Task<Card> UnfreezeAsync(Guid cardId, CancellationToken ct = default);
    Task<Card> CancelAsync(Guid cardId, CancellationToken ct = default);
    Task<CardAuthorisation> AuthoriseAsync(Guid cardId, decimal amount, string merchant, CancellationToken ct = default); }  // card network: no owner check
  sealed class CardService(BankDbContext db, ILedger ledger, IAccountService accounts, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock, IEventBus bus) : ICardService
BankDbContext gets: DbSet<Card> Cards
HTTP: POST api/cards, POST api/cards/{id}/freeze|unfreeze|cancel (Customer policy); POST api/cards/{id}/authorise (Staff policy, stands in for the card network)
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Cards/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs`
- `src/Bank.Api/Program.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ Customers can get a debit card for one of their accounts, freeze it (for example when it is lost), unfreeze it, and cancel it for good. The card network asks the bank to authorise card payments: the bank approves only if the card is active, the amount is within the card's per-transaction limit (2,000 in the account's currency) and the account has the money; approved amounts move to the bank's Suspense account until settlement. Declines are answers, not errors. The full card number is personal data; only the last four digits may be shown or sent.

# PR-6: PR-6: Term deposits module (open, mature, and early break)

**Story.** As a bank customer, I want to lock funds into a 3, 6, or 12-month term deposit at a fixed annual interest rate and either collect my principal plus simple interest at maturity or break the deposit early to recover my principal only, so that I can earn predictable interest on locked savings.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Module and persistence follow Nordbank conventions: Bank.Modules.Deposits with Domain, Application, Api layers, DepositsModule.AddDepositsModule registered in Program.cs above // MODULES:, and DbSet<TermDeposit> TermDeposits registered in BankDbContext above // TABLES:.
- [ ] Public contract matches the agreed types and signatures in Bank.Modules.Deposits.Domain (DepositStatus, TermDeposit with parameterless constructor and private setter on Status, DepositOpened, DepositClosed) and Bank.Modules.Deposits.Application (IDepositService, DepositService).
- [ ] Opening a deposit via POST api/deposits (Policies.Customer) or IDepositService.OpenAsync verifies via IAccountService.IsOwnerAsync that ICurrentUser.UserId owns accountId; non-owners throw UnauthorizedAccessException.
- [ ] OpenAsync validates principal >= 500m and termMonths is 3 (2.0% annual rate), 6 (2.5% annual rate), or 12 (3.0% annual rate); any principal below 500m or other term length throws ArgumentException.
- [ ] OpenAsync derives CustomerId from ICurrentUser.UserId and Currency from the source account, transfers principal from accountId to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.DepositHolding, currency) via ILedger.PostTransferAsync, sets OpenedAt = clock.UtcNow, MaturesAt = OpenedAt.AddMonths(termMonths), Status = DepositStatus.Open, InterestPaid = 0m, persists the TermDeposit, and publishes DepositOpened.
- [ ] Maturing a deposit via POST api/deposits/{id}/mature (Policies.Staff) or IDepositService.MatureAsync performs no owner check and throws InvalidOperationException if the deposit is not Open or if clock.UtcNow < MaturesAt.
- [ ] MatureAsync computes simple interest using decimal arithmetic as Math.Round(Principal * (AnnualRatePercent / 100m) * TermMonths / 12m, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero), transfers Principal from DepositHolding to AccountId and InterestPaid from InterestExpense to AccountId in the deposit's currency via ILedger.PostTransferAsync, transitions Status to DepositStatus.Matured, sets InterestPaid, and publishes DepositClosed with Early = false.
- [ ] Breaking a deposit via POST api/deposits/{id}/break (Policies.Customer) or IDepositService.BreakAsync checks that ICurrentUser.UserId owns the deposit (throwing UnauthorizedAccessException otherwise) and throws InvalidOperationException if Status is not DepositStatus.Open.
- [ ] BreakAsync transfers Principal only from DepositHolding to AccountId via ILedger.PostTransferAsync, transitions Status to DepositStatus.BrokenEarly with InterestPaid = 0m, and publishes DepositClosed with Early = true.
- [ ] All time checks use IClock.UtcNow (never DateTime.Now or DateTimeOffset.UtcNow), all currency movement goes through ILedger.PostTransferAsync without editing Account.Balance directly, and no PII is included in domain events or logs.
- [ ] Automated xUnit tests verify: 3/6/12-month rate mapping and interest rounding half away from zero, principal < 500 and invalid term rejection, owner enforcement on open and break, Staff-only maturity enforcement, rejection of premature maturity, rejection of breaking or maturing an already closed deposit, and ledger balances across Customer, DepositHolding, and InterestExpense accounts.

## Out of scope
- Background scheduler or automatic timer job to invoke MatureAsync automatically at maturity
- Partial withdrawals from an active term deposit or topping up an existing deposit
- Early-break penalty fees beyond forfeiting accrued interest
- Automatic renewal or rollover of principal and interest into a new term deposit at maturity
- Custom or promotional interest rates and terms other than 3, 6, or 12 months
- Query/GET endpoints for listing or fetching term deposits
- Tax withholding or reporting on interest paid

## Risks
- Double-payout or race condition: concurrent MatureAsync and BreakAsync calls (or repeated calls) on the same Open deposit could pay out principal or interest twice if state transitions and persistence are not strictly guarded.
- Partial failure between ledger and database: if ILedger.PostTransferAsync succeeds for principal or interest but saving the TermDeposit status fails (or vice versa), bank internal accounts (DepositHolding, InterestExpense) and deposit state will become inconsistent.
- Interest calculation defects: integer division on TermMonths / 12, omitting division by 100m on AnnualRatePercent, or using banker's rounding instead of MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero would miscalculate customer payouts.
- Authorization bypass: allowing a Customer to invoke the Staff mature endpoint or failing to verify deposit/account ownership on open and break could allow unauthorized locking of another user's funds or premature interest payout.
- Premature maturity or test flakiness: bypassing IClock or evaluating MaturesAt inaccurately could allow customers to collect unearned interest before the term ends.
- Currency mismatch: using BankSettings.DefaultCurrency instead of the source account's Currency when addressing DepositHolding or InterestExpense would fail or corrupt multi-currency ledger entries.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Modules.Deposits.Domain:
  enum DepositStatus { Open, Matured, BrokenEarly }
  sealed class TermDeposit { Guid Id; string CustomerId; Guid AccountId; decimal Principal; string Currency; int TermMonths;
                             decimal AnnualRatePercent; DateTimeOffset OpenedAt; DateTimeOffset MaturesAt; DepositStatus Status; decimal InterestPaid }
  sealed record DepositOpened(Guid DepositId, string CustomerId, decimal Principal, int TermMonths, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record DepositClosed(Guid DepositId, string CustomerId, decimal InterestPaid, bool Early, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
namespace Bank.Modules.Deposits.Application:
  interface IDepositService {
    Task<TermDeposit> OpenAsync(Guid accountId, decimal principal, int termMonths, CancellationToken ct = default);
        // not owner -> UnauthorizedAccessException; principal < 500 or term not 3/6/12 -> ArgumentException
    Task<TermDeposit> MatureAsync(Guid depositId, CancellationToken ct = default);   // before MaturesAt or not Open -> InvalidOperationException (runs as a bank job: no owner check)
    Task<TermDeposit> BreakAsync(Guid depositId, CancellationToken ct = default); }  // owner only; not Open -> InvalidOperationException
  sealed class DepositService(BankDbContext db, ILedger ledger, IAccountService accounts, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock, IEventBus bus) : IDepositService
BankDbContext gets: DbSet<TermDeposit> TermDeposits
HTTP: POST api/deposits, POST api/deposits/{id}/break (Customer); POST api/deposits/{id}/mature (Staff)
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Deposits/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs`
- `src/Bank.Api/Program.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ Customers can lock money in a term deposit for 3, 6 or 12 months at 2.0%, 2.5% or 3.0% a year; the minimum is 500. Opening moves the money from their account to the bank's DepositHolding account. At maturity the customer gets the principal back plus simple interest (principal x rate x months / 12, rounded to cents half away from zero) paid from InterestExpense. Breaking a deposit before maturity returns the principal only. Only the owner can open or break.

# PR-7: PR-7: Loans module with annuity calculation and four-eyes approval

**Story.** As a verified customer, I want to apply for a fixed-rate loan disbursed to one of my accounts and be notified of the decision, so that I can borrow funds safely while a different loan officer independently reviews and approves or rejects my application.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Module Bank.Modules.Loans is implemented with Api, Application, Domain layers, LoansModule registration in Program.cs, and DbSet<Loan> Loans added to BankDbContext.
- [ ] Loan entity in Bank.Modules.Loans.Domain owns Status (LoanStatus: Submitted, Rejected, Disbursed) with a private setter, transitions state only via domain methods that validate current status, and includes a parameterless constructor and public settable non-status properties.
- [ ] POST api/loans (Policies.Customer) delegates to ILoanService.ApplyAsync using ICurrentUser.UserId as CustomerId and IClock.UtcNow as AppliedAt, ignoring any user id supplied in request bodies.
- [ ] ILoanService.ApplyAsync validates that Principal is between 1000m and 50000m inclusive and TermMonths is between 6 and 120 inclusive, throwing ArgumentException when out of range.
- [ ] ILoanService.ApplyAsync verifies via IAccountService.IsOwnerAsync that DisbursementAccountId belongs to the caller, throwing UnauthorizedAccessException if not owned.
- [ ] ILoanService.ApplyAsync sets AnnualRatePercent to 5.5m and calculates MonthlyPayment using the standard monthly annuity formula P * r / (1 - (1 + r)^(-n)) with monthly rate r = 0.055m / 12m, rounded to 2 decimal places using Math.Round(value, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero).
- [ ] ILoanService.ApplyAsync persists the Loan in Submitted status and publishes LoanSubmitted via IEventBus.PublishAsync.
- [ ] GET api/loans/{id} (Policies.Customer) calls ILoanService.GetAsync, which throws KeyNotFoundException if the loan does not exist, and throws UnauthorizedAccessException if the caller is neither the Loan.CustomerId nor in Roles.LoanOfficer.
- [ ] POST api/loans/{id}/approve (Policies.LoanOfficer) calls ILoanService.ApproveAsync, which throws KeyNotFoundException if not found, UnauthorizedAccessException if the caller is not in Roles.LoanOfficer or if caller UserId equals Loan.CustomerId (four-eyes check), and InvalidOperationException if Loan.Status is not Submitted.
- [ ] ILoanService.ApproveAsync transitions the loan to Disbursed, records DecidedBy (caller UserId) and optional DecisionNote, resolves the disbursement account currency via IAccountService.GetAsync, and transfers Principal from BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.LoanFunding, account.Currency) to Loan.DisbursementAccountId via ILedger.PostTransferAsync.
- [ ] ILoanService.ApproveAsync publishes LoanApproved via IEventBus.PublishAsync and notifies the customer via INotifier with a message containing no personal data (no name, email, account details, or other PII).
- [ ] POST api/loans/{id}/reject (Policies.LoanOfficer) calls ILoanService.RejectAsync, which enforces the same LoanOfficer role, four-eyes check (UnauthorizedAccessException), and Submitted status check (InvalidOperationException), and throws ArgumentException if reason is null, empty, or whitespace.
- [ ] ILoanService.RejectAsync transitions the loan to Rejected, records DecidedBy and DecisionNote, publishes LoanRejected via IEventBus.PublishAsync, and notifies the customer via INotifier without any personal data in the message.
- [ ] Automated xUnit tests cover range validation, annuity rounding, ownership enforcement, four-eyes rejection of self-approval/self-rejection, invalid state transitions, ledger disbursement in the account currency, domain event publishing, and PII-free notifications.

## Out of scope
- Loan repayment processing, installment collection, or amortization schedule generation.
- Collection or search endpoints such as GET api/loans for listing or filtering multiple loans.
- Variable interest rates, custom interest rates per customer, credit scoring, or external KYC verification workflows.
- Cross-currency loan disbursement or FX conversion between LoanFunding and the disbursement account.
- Early loan payoff, loan restructuring, or cancellation of a submitted loan by the customer.

## Risks
- Four-eyes control bypass: if a loan officer can approve or reject their own loan, internal fraud or unauthorized fund disbursement becomes possible.
- Double disbursement race condition: concurrent approval requests could disburse principal multiple times if the Submitted status transition and persistence are not atomic.
- Currency mismatch or ledger failure: using the wrong currency for BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.LoanFunding, currency) instead of the disbursement account's currency will fail or corrupt accounting balances.
- Annuity calculation or rounding error: using floating-point math instead of decimal or incorrect rounding mode could misstate monthly payments and cause regulatory or customer disputes.
- PII leakage: including customer identifiers, names, or account information in INotifier messages or logs violates bank privacy and compliance rules.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Modules.Loans.Domain:
  enum LoanStatus { Submitted, Rejected, Disbursed }
  sealed class Loan { Guid Id; string CustomerId; Guid DisbursementAccountId; decimal Principal; int TermMonths; decimal AnnualRatePercent;
                      decimal MonthlyPayment; LoanStatus Status; string? DecidedBy; string? DecisionNote; DateTimeOffset AppliedAt }
  sealed record LoanSubmitted(Guid LoanId, string CustomerId, decimal Principal, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record LoanApproved(Guid LoanId, string CustomerId, decimal Principal, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record LoanRejected(Guid LoanId, string CustomerId, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
namespace Bank.Modules.Loans.Application:
  sealed record LoanApplication(Guid DisbursementAccountId, decimal Principal, int TermMonths)
  interface ILoanService {
    Task<Loan> ApplyAsync(LoanApplication application, CancellationToken ct = default);
        // out-of-range amount/term -> ArgumentException; account not owned by caller -> UnauthorizedAccessException
    Task<Loan> GetAsync(Guid loanId, CancellationToken ct = default);     // unknown -> KeyNotFoundException; not owner and not loan officer -> UnauthorizedAccessException
    Task<Loan> ApproveAsync(Guid loanId, string? note, CancellationToken ct = default);
        // not a loan officer, or the officer is the borrower -> UnauthorizedAccessException; not Submitted -> InvalidOperationException
    Task<Loan> RejectAsync(Guid loanId, string reason, CancellationToken ct = default); }   // same rules; empty reason -> ArgumentException
  sealed class LoanService(BankDbContext db, ILedger ledger, IAccountService accounts, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock,
                           IEventBus bus, INotifier notifier) : ILoanService
BankDbContext gets: DbSet<Loan> Loans
HTTP: POST api/loans, GET api/loans/{id} (Customer); POST api/loans/{id}/approve|reject (LoanOfficer)
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Loans/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs`
- `src/Bank.Api/Program.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ A verified customer applies for a loan of 1,000-50,000 over 6-120 months, paid out to one of their own accounts, at 5.5% a year. The monthly payment uses the annuity formula, rounded to cents half away from zero. Customers can see their own loans; loan officers can see all. A loan officer approves or rejects a submitted loan with a note; an officer must never decide on their own loan. Approval pays the principal from the bank's LoanFunding account (in the account's currency) and the loan becomes Disbursed; the customer is notified without any personal data in the message.

# PR-8: PR-8: Monthly account statements (API and StatementService)

**Story.** As a bank customer or authorized staff member, I want to retrieve a monthly account statement for a given calendar month in UTC, showing the opening balance, chronological ledger entries with running balances, and the closing balance, so that account activity and balances can be accurately reviewed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Implement Bank.Modules.Statements following the module layout (Api, Application, StatementsModule) and register AddStatementsModule in Program.cs above the // MODULES: marker.
- [ ] Expose the agreed public contract in namespace Bank.Modules.Statements.Application: StatementLine(DateTimeOffset At, decimal Amount, decimal BalanceAfter, string Reference), Statement(Guid AccountId, int Year, int Month, string Currency, decimal OpeningBalance, decimal ClosingBalance, IReadOnlyList<StatementLine> Lines), IStatementService with ForMonthAsync(Guid accountId, int year, int month, CancellationToken ct = default), and StatementService(ILedger ledger, IAccountService accounts, ICurrentUser user).
- [ ] Expose GET api/accounts/{id}/statements/{year}/{month} on a controller decorated with [ApiController] and [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Customer)], returning HTTP 200 OK with the Statement payload.
- [ ] Month boundaries are strictly UTC: include entries with timestamp >= YYYY-MM-01T00:00:00Z and < (YYYY-MM-01 + 1 month)T00:00:00Z; entries at exactly 00:00:00Z on the 1st of the next month belong to the next month and are excluded.
- [ ] Invalid calendar inputs (such as month < 1 or > 12, or year < 1 or > 9999) are rejected with ArgumentOutOfRangeException (mapped to HTTP 400 Bad Request).
- [ ] OpeningBalance equals the sum of all ledger entries for the account strictly before YYYY-MM-01T00:00:00Z (0.00m if none), rounded to 2 decimal places using Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero).
- [ ] Lines are ordered chronologically by At ascending, and each line's BalanceAfter equals the prior balance plus that line's signed Amount, rounded to 2 decimal places with MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero.
- [ ] ClosingBalance equals OpeningBalance plus the sum of all Line Amounts in the month (when there are no entries in the month, Lines is empty and ClosingBalance equals OpeningBalance), and Statement.Currency matches the account's currency.
- [ ] If the account does not exist, ForMonthAsync throws KeyNotFoundException (mapped to HTTP 404 Not Found).
- [ ] If the current user is neither the owner of the account (via IAccountService.IsOwnerAsync) nor in a staff role (Teller, LoanOfficer, ComplianceOfficer, or Admin in Bank.Modules.Auth.Roles), ForMonthAsync throws UnauthorizedAccessException (mapped to HTTP 403 Forbidden).
- [ ] Unauthenticated requests to GET api/accounts/{id}/statements/{year}/{month} are rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
- [ ] Statement generation is strictly read-only: it never modifies Account.Balance and never posts ledger transfers.

## Out of scope
- Exporting or rendering statements as PDF, CSV, HTML, or other downloadable file formats.
- Persisting or caching generated monthly statement snapshots in a database table or emailing statements to customers.
- Custom date range queries, rolling 30-day statements, or timezone conversions outside UTC.
- Pagination, sorting options, or filtering of statement lines by amount or reference.
- Charging statement fees or performing currency conversions.

## Risks
- Broken object-level authorization (IDOR) if ownership or staff-role verification is flawed, allowing a customer to view another customer's balances and transaction references.
- Off-by-one boundary bugs at month rollover (e.g., using <= instead of < for next month's 1st at 00:00 UTC or using local time instead of UTC), causing entries at midnight UTC to be duplicated across months or omitted and breaking OpeningBalance + month entries = ClosingBalance.
- Non-deterministic line ordering when multiple ledger entries share the same At timestamp, producing inconsistent BalanceAfter values across calls.
- Using Account.Balance directly instead of computing OpeningBalance and ClosingBalance from ledger history, which would fail for past months or after subsequent transactions.
- Precision or rounding discrepancies if non-decimal arithmetic is used or Math.Round(..., 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) is omitted.
- Performance degradation if an account has a large ledger history and entries are not filtered or queried efficiently.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Modules.Statements.Application:
  sealed record StatementLine(DateTimeOffset At, decimal Amount, decimal BalanceAfter, string Reference)
  sealed record Statement(Guid AccountId, int Year, int Month, string Currency, decimal OpeningBalance, decimal ClosingBalance,
                          IReadOnlyList<StatementLine> Lines)
  interface IStatementService { Task<Statement> ForMonthAsync(Guid accountId, int year, int month, CancellationToken ct = default); }
      // unknown account -> KeyNotFoundException; not owner and not staff (teller, loan officer, compliance officer, admin) -> UnauthorizedAccessException
  sealed class StatementService(ILedger ledger, IAccountService accounts, ICurrentUser user) : IStatementService
HTTP: GET api/accounts/{id}/statements/{year}/{month} (Customer)
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Statements/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Program.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ A customer can get a statement for one of their accounts for a calendar month: the opening balance, every entry of the month with the balance after it, and the closing balance. The month runs from the 1st at 00:00 UTC up to (not including) the 1st of the next month. Opening balance + the month's entries = closing balance. Staff can read any statement; customers only their own.

# PR-9: PR-9: Update BankSettings for Swedish launch (SEK default currency and 5,000 EUR daily transfer limit)

**Story.** As the bank preparing for the Swedish launch and complying with regulatory guidance, I want Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings updated so that new accounts default to SEK and the daily transfer limit is reduced from 10,000 to 5,000 EUR equivalent for all customers, with no other behavioral changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings has DefaultCurrency set to "SEK" (changed from "EUR").
- [ ] Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings has DailyTransferLimit set to 5_000m (decimal 5000.00, changed from 10_000m).
- [ ] Bank.Shared.Settings.BankSettings SupportedCurrencies remains unchanged (EUR, SEK, USD).
- [ ] When an authenticated Customer (or authorized Staff/Admin role per existing account creation policy) creates a new account without specifying a currency, the created account uses DefaultCurrency ("SEK").
- [ ] When an authenticated Customer (or authorized role) creates a new account explicitly specifying another supported currency (such as "EUR" or "USD"), the account is still created in that requested supported currency.
- [ ] Existing accounts retain their previously assigned currencies and balances; only newly created accounts without an explicit currency default to "SEK".
- [ ] For any Customer initiating transfers, the cumulative daily transfer limit check enforces 5_000m EUR equivalent (using decimal arithmetic and Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero) where EUR equivalent conversion applies): a transfer causing the daily total to equal 5,000.00 EUR equivalent succeeds, while a transfer causing the daily total to exceed 5,000.00 EUR equivalent (e.g., 5,000.01 EUR equivalent or a second transfer pushing the UTC day total above 5,000.00) is rejected with the existing daily limit validation error and posts no ledger movement.
- [ ] Authorization policies, roles, current user identity resolution via ICurrentUser, and UTC day boundary calculation via IClock remain unchanged; no customer or role can bypass the 5,000m daily transfer limit unless already permitted by existing policy.
- [ ] All existing modules and tests that depend on BankSettings continue to pass after updating any test assertions that previously assumed EUR default or 10,000m limit.

## Out of scope
- Converting or migrating existing customer accounts from EUR or USD to SEK.
- Adding new currencies or removing existing currencies from SupportedCurrencies.
- Introducing per-customer, tiered, or role-specific daily transfer limits.
- Adding an API endpoint or UI to edit BankSettings at runtime.
- Modifying FX conversion rates, fee schedules, interest rates, or loan rules.
- Changing account creation or transfer authorization policies or adding new user roles.

## Risks
- Any module that hardcoded "EUR" or 10_000m instead of injecting BankSettings would create accounts in the wrong currency or allow transfers above the 5,000 EUR regulatory cap, causing a compliance breach.
- Existing automated tests or downstream integrations that assert "EUR" as the default account currency or 10,000 as the transfer limit will break unless aligned with BankSettings.
- Rounding differences during non-EUR to EUR equivalent conversion near the 5,000.00 boundary could cause slight limit overruns or unexpected rejections if AwayFromZero cent rounding is not applied consistently.
- Customers attempting legitimate transfers between 5,000.01 and 10,000.00 EUR equivalent immediately after deployment will be rejected, risking support incidents if not communicated prior to launch.

## Public contract
```
BankSettings: DefaultCurrency = "SEK"; DailyTransferLimit = 5_000m; SupportedCurrencies unchanged.
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Shared/Settings/BankSettings.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ We launch in Sweden next week. New accounts must default to SEK instead of EUR, and following the regulator's guidance the daily transfer limit drops from 10,000 to 5,000 (EUR equivalent) for all customers. Nothing else changes.

# PR-10: PR-10: Centralize cent rounding in shared Bank.Shared.Money.MoneyMath helper

**Story.** As a bank developer, I want one shared MoneyMath.ToCents rounding helper used across the Fx, Fees, Deposits, and Loans modules so that cent rounding is defined in a single place without changing any amounts seen by customers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A public static class MoneyMath is defined in namespace Bank.Shared.Money (in its own file, one public type per file) with signature public static decimal ToCents(decimal amount).
- [ ] MoneyMath.ToCents rounds decimal values to 2 decimal places using MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero: ToCents(2.345m) returns 2.35m, ToCents(-2.345m) returns -2.35m, ToCents(0.005m) returns 0.01m, ToCents(-0.005m) returns -0.01m, ToCents(0m) returns 0.00m, and exact-cent amounts like 12.34m remain 12.34m.
- [ ] All cent-rounding calls in the Fx, Fees, Deposits, and Loans modules use MoneyMath.ToCents, and no direct Math.Round(..., 2, ...) or duplicate cent-rounding helper remains in those four modules.
- [ ] Rounding occurs at the exact same calculation steps as before the refactor so that every customer-facing and ledger-posted amount in Fx conversions, Fee charges, Deposit interest/operations, and Loan calculations is identical to pre-refactor amounts.
- [ ] Existing role-based authorization policies (Customer, Staff, LoanOfficer, Compliance, Admin), ownership checks, and error behaviors (such as 400/401/403/404 responses) in Fx, Fees, Deposits, and Loans remain completely unchanged.
- [ ] Unit tests cover MoneyMath.ToCents for positive, negative, zero, midpoint away-from-zero, and unchanged 2-decimal inputs, and existing plus regression tests in Fx, Fees, Deposits, and Loans pass with identical monetary results.

## Out of scope
- Changing rounding precision, currency-specific decimal places (e.g., 0 or 3 decimals), or midpoint rounding strategy.
- Refactoring rounding in modules other than Fx, Fees, Deposits, and Loans.
- Adding extra methods or types to Bank.Shared.Money beyond MoneyMath.ToCents(decimal amount) (such as Money value objects, currency formatting, or allocation helpers).
- Modifying API contracts, DTOs, database tables, authorization rules, or adding new NuGet packages.

## Risks
- Implementing MoneyMath.ToCents with MidpointRounding.ToEven (the default in Math.Round) instead of MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero would misround half-cent amounts (e.g., 2.345 to 2.34 instead of 2.35) and cause 1-cent discrepancies in customer balances or bank income accounts.
- Changing the order or point at which rounding is applied during Fx, Fees, Deposits, or Loans calculations could subtly alter amounts charged to or paid to customers.
- Missing one or more inline rounding expressions in Fx, Fees, Deposits, or Loans would leave inconsistent rounding behavior across the codebase.
- Mishandling negative values (such as reversals, fees, or adjustments) could violate symmetric half-away-from-zero behavior (-2.345 to -2.35) and create ledger posting mismatches.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Shared.Money:
  static class MoneyMath { static decimal ToCents(decimal amount); }   // rounds to 2 decimals, half away from zero (2.345 -> 2.35, -2.345 -> -2.35)
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Shared/Money/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Fx/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Fees/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Deposits/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Loans/**`

_Brief from the product owner:_ Rounding to cents is written separately in several modules. Create one shared helper and use it in the Fx, Fees, Deposits and Loans modules. This is a refactor: no customer may see a different amount afterwards.

# PR-11: PR-11: Enforce idempotent payment processing for retries and concurrent requests

**Story.** As a Nordbank customer using the mobile app, I want retried or concurrent payment requests with the same idempotency key to be processed only once so that I am never charged twice when a request times out.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No public method signatures are changed; IPaymentService.PayAsync retains its existing signature, authorization checks (Policies.Customer and ICurrentUser.UserId), and account ownership checks via IAccountService.IsOwnerAsync.
- [ ] The Payment database table enforces a composite unique index on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) via EF Core configuration so duplicate keys for the same customer are rejected at the database level.
- [ ] CustomerId used for idempotency scoping is always sourced from ICurrentUser.UserId and never from request DTOs.
- [ ] When IPaymentService.PayAsync is called sequentially by the same customer with an IdempotencyKey that already exists for that CustomerId, it returns the existing first payment without calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync or moving money again.
- [ ] When two requests with the same CustomerId and IdempotencyKey execute concurrently, at most one payment record is persisted and ILedger.PostTransferAsync is called at most once (with decimal amount rounded using Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)); the second request handles the database unique constraint violation and returns the existing first payment rather than failing with an unhandled exception.
- [ ] Idempotency keys are strictly scoped per customer: two different customers submitting the same IdempotencyKey each succeed independently with their own payments, and one customer cannot read another customer's payment by reusing their IdempotencyKey.
- [ ] If the first attempt fails before committing a valid payment (for example, validation error, insufficient balance, or unauthorized account), no idempotency record locks out a subsequent valid request or no money is moved via ILedger.
- [ ] Automated xUnit tests verify sequential retry behavior, concurrent identical requests against SQLite enforcing the unique index, cross-customer key isolation, and that ILedger.PostTransferAsync is invoked exactly once for duplicate requests.

## Out of scope
- Changing the public signature of IPaymentService.PayAsync, HTTP controller routes, or DTO contracts.
- Adding idempotency key expiration, TTL policies, or background cleanup jobs.
- Validating or rejecting payload mismatches when the same idempotency key is reused with a different amount or target account (returning 409/422).
- Introducing distributed locks, external caching (such as Redis), or new NuGet packages.
- Data remediation or refunds for historical duplicate payments referenced in support ticket #4711.

## Risks
- Calling ILedger.PostTransferAsync before atomically persisting or reserving the unique (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) database record would allow two concurrent threads to both transfer money before one fails on the unique constraint.
- Catching DbUpdateException too broadly without verifying it is a unique constraint violation on (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) could mask real persistence errors or return incorrect responses.
- Creating the unique index on IdempotencyKey alone rather than (CustomerId, IdempotencyKey) would allow one customer's key to block another customer's payment or leak another customer's payment data.
- Re-querying the existing payment within a poisoned EF Core change tracker or uncommitted transaction after a unique constraint failure in SQLite could cause stale state or secondary exceptions.
- Sourcing CustomerId from a request payload instead of ICurrentUser.UserId would allow spoofing and unauthorized access to another customer's payment result.

## Public contract
```
No public signature changes. IPaymentService.PayAsync keeps its behaviour; a repeated key returns the first payment.
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Payments/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Data/BankDbContext.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ Support ticket #4711: a customer was charged twice for one payment after the mobile app retried a request that had timed out. Make sure a payment request with the same idempotency key from the same customer can never move money twice, also when two identical requests arrive at the same moment. The database must enforce it as well (a unique index on customer + idempotency key).

prs.head: de5c0e1b2129aa9969f4056f72230b8ba71ef709
prs.issue:
# PR-12: PR-12: Hold large payments to new payees for compliance review

**Story.** As a compliance officer at Nordbank, I want outgoing payments of 5,000 EUR equivalent or more to a payee account the customer has not paid before to be placed in Held status with funds moved to Suspense until a compliance officer releases or rejects them, so that potential fraud is stopped before funds leave the bank.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When a customer initiates a payment whose amount in EUR equivalent is 5,000.00 EUR or more (calculated using decimal arithmetic and rounded with Math.Round(x, 2, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)) to a destination account that the customer has no prior Completed payment to, PaymentService sets the payment status to Held via a domain state-transition method on Payment (with a private setter on status).
- [ ] When a payment is held, ILedger.PostTransferAsync transfers (amount + fee) in the payment's currency from the payer's account to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, currency); no funds are transferred to the payee or FeeIncome while Held.
- [ ] When a payment is held, PaymentService publishes PaymentHeld(PaymentId, CustomerId, Amount, Currency, clock.UtcNow) via IEventBus and notifies the customer via INotifier (injected after IFeeCalculator) that the payment is being checked, without including any PII.
- [ ] Payments under 5,000.00 EUR equivalent, or payments to an account the customer has previously completed a payment to, are not held and execute normally.
- [ ] PaymentReviewService implements IPaymentReviewService with constructor (BankDbContext db, ILedger ledger, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock, IEventBus bus, INotifier notifier).
- [ ] All IPaymentReviewService methods (HeldAsync, ReleaseAsync, RejectAsync) enforce that ICurrentUser is in the Compliance role, throwing UnauthorizedAccessException otherwise.
- [ ] HeldAsync returns all payments currently in Held status.
- [ ] ReleaseAsync verifies the payment exists (throwing KeyNotFoundException if not), verifies the payment status is Held (throwing InvalidOperationException otherwise), and verifies payment.CustomerId is not equal to ICurrentUser.UserId (throwing UnauthorizedAccessException if an officer attempts to release their own payment).
- [ ] On ReleaseAsync, ILedger.PostTransferAsync transfers amount from BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, currency) to the payee's account and (if fee > 0) transfers fee from Suspense to BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.FeeIncome, currency), transitions the payment status from Held to Completed, publishes PaymentReleased(PaymentId, user.UserId, clock.UtcNow), and notifies the customer via INotifier.
- [ ] RejectAsync validates that reason is non-empty (throwing ArgumentException if null or whitespace), verifies the payment exists (KeyNotFoundException if not), verifies status is Held (InvalidOperationException if not), and verifies payment.CustomerId != user.UserId (UnauthorizedAccessException on own payment).
- [ ] On RejectAsync, ILedger.PostTransferAsync transfers (amount + fee) from BankAccounts.For(BankAccountKind.Suspense, currency) back to the payer's account, transitions the payment status from Held to Rejected, publishes PaymentRejected(PaymentId, user.UserId, clock.UtcNow), and notifies the customer via INotifier without exposing PII.
- [ ] HTTP endpoints GET api/payments/held, POST api/payments/{id}/release, and POST api/payments/{id}/reject are protected with [Authorize(Policy = Policies.Compliance)], use ICurrentUser rather than request-body user IDs, and use IClock.UtcNow for all timestamps.

## Out of scope
- Per-customer or admin-configurable review thresholds or payee allowlists/whitelists.
- Automatic expiry or timeout of Held payments if no compliance officer acts.
- Four-eyes or multi-officer approval workflows for releasing or rejecting a payment.
- Customer-initiated cancellation or editing of a payment while it is in Held status.
- Pagination, filtering, or bulk release/reject endpoints on GET api/payments/held.
- Cross-currency settlement inside Suspense (all transfers for a payment occur in the payment's single currency).

## Risks
- Concurrent release or reject calls on the same Held payment could result in double payouts from Suspense or overdrafting the Suspense account if state transitions and database updates are not protected against concurrency.
- Non-atomic failure between ledger transfers (Suspense to payee, Suspense to FeeIncome, or Suspense back to payer) and saving the updated Payment status could leave ledger balances and payment status out of sync.
- Rounding or FX conversion errors near the 5,000.00 EUR boundary could allow large fraudulent payments to bypass review or leave residual cents stranded in Suspense.
- Counting prior Held, Rejected, or Failed payments as 'previously paid' would allow an attacker to bypass review by submitting a failed or rejected payment to the same payee first.
- Omitting the self-decision or role check in PaymentReviewService could allow a compliance officer to approve their own payment or an unauthorized caller to invoke review methods directly.
- Including customer PII or raw rejection text containing personal data in PaymentHeld, PaymentReleased, PaymentRejected events, logs, or notifications would violate bank privacy rules.

## Public contract
```
namespace Bank.Modules.Payments.Domain:
  sealed record PaymentHeld(Guid PaymentId, string CustomerId, decimal Amount, string Currency, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record PaymentReleased(Guid PaymentId, string ReleasedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
  sealed record PaymentRejected(Guid PaymentId, string RejectedBy, DateTimeOffset OccurredAt) : IDomainEvent
namespace Bank.Modules.Payments.Application:
  interface IPaymentReviewService {
    Task<IReadOnlyList<Payment>> HeldAsync(CancellationToken ct = default);
    Task<Payment> ReleaseAsync(Guid paymentId, CancellationToken ct = default);   // compliance officer only; own payment -> UnauthorizedAccessException; not Held -> InvalidOperationException
    Task<Payment> RejectAsync(Guid paymentId, string reason, CancellationToken ct = default); }
  sealed class PaymentReviewService(BankDbContext db, ILedger ledger, ICurrentUser user, IClock clock, IEventBus bus, INotifier notifier) : IPaymentReviewService
PaymentService gets INotifier as a constructor argument (after IFeeCalculator).
HTTP: GET api/payments/held, POST api/payments/{id}/release|reject (Compliance)
```

## Allowed scope
- `src/Bank.Api/Modules/Payments/**`
- `src/Bank.Api/Program.cs`

_Brief from the product owner:_ To fight fraud, a payment of 5,000 EUR or more (EUR equivalent) to an account the customer has never paid before is held: the money (amount + fee) leaves the payer's account and waits in the bank's Suspense account, the payment status is Held, and the customer is told it is being checked. A compliance officer then releases it (the payee is credited) or rejects it (the payer gets everything back). Officers cannot decide on their own payments.
